newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire opposition protest closes much of Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Zaire opposition protest closes much of Kinshasa.

text.p: An opposition strike call closed down much of Zaire's capital Kinshasa on Monday, with the central bank open but many shops and businesses closed, witnesses said.

Soldiers in military vehicles patrolled potential flashpoints and civil guards deployed at petrol stations which mostly stayed shut. In one residential district youths set fire to tyres but there was no early report of violence.
The main opposition of Sacred Union of the Radical Opposition (USOR) of Etienne Tshisekedi called the protest to demand the removal of Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo.

The opposition, which has called for negotiations with rebels in the east, attacked Kengo's conduct of the war and accused him of stalling on organising promised elections as a way of hanging on to power.
The central bank was open but the business district of the capital was quiet. Shops and public and private companies remained closed as did some government offices.
The central market was closed with its stalls empty. Occasional hawkers and vendors laid out their wares on the outskirts of the market.
Tshisekedi, removed from the office of prime minister by President Mobutu Sese Seko in 1993, has never accepted Kengo's appointment to the job the following year.
The radical opposition called a similar protest in 1995. It flopped with businesses and government offices working normally.
